items.label: What is the threat model's identifier, title, version, and last-revision date, and is it under version control?
Who owns this threat model and which authors/contributors produced it?
When was the model last reviewed/approved by whom, and what triggers or schedule drives the next review?
What system/release is in scope, what is explicitly out of scope, and what is the document status (draft/reviewed/approved)?
What key assumptions, constraints, and pre-existing security controls frame the system's context?
Where and how is the system deployed (environments, hosting model, network exposure)?
What external systems, services, and dependencies does the system interact with at the context level?
What does the system do, what business/mission purpose does it serve, and who are its users?
What are the system's protectable assets (data, credentials, keys, intellectual property, infrastructure, reputation)?
Who owns or is accountable for each asset?
Which CIA (confidentiality/integrity/availability) and other security objectives apply to each asset?
What is the business value and the impact of compromise for each asset?
What handling, encryption, and access requirements apply to each classification level (at rest and in transit)?
What classification levels (e.g. public/internal/confidential/restricted) exist and how is each data type assigned a level?
What are the retention and disposal/deletion requirements per classification level?
Which specific sensitive data types (PII, PHI, financial, secrets) are present and how are they tagged?
Who/what are the actors and principals (human users, admins, services, external parties, attackers) interacting with the system?
What roles and privilege levels does each actor hold, and what is the highest privilege available?
Which adversarial threat agents are modeled and what capabilities/motivations are attributed to them?
What trust level is assigned to each actor (trusted, semi-trusted, untrusted/anonymous)?
What controls (authentication, validation, authorization) enforce each trust boundary crossing?
Which data flows and components cross each trust boundary, and what is being trusted at the crossing?
Where are the trust boundaries in the system (between zones of differing trust, privilege, or ownership)?
Where do privilege-level or security-context changes occur across boundaries?
Do the diagrams depict all components, data stores, flows, and external entities in scope?
Are appropriate levels of decomposition (context vs detailed/DFD levels) provided?
Does a current architecture/data-flow diagram exist that matches the deployed system?
Do diagrams include a legend and consistent labels that trace to the component/flow inventory?
Are flows annotated with protocols, ports, data classification, and authentication on each connection?
Are trust boundaries explicitly drawn/annotated on the diagrams?
What internal/external dependencies does each component have?
Is every component (services, processes, libraries, infrastructure elements) enumerated with a unique identifier?
For each component, what is its responsibility, technology/runtime, and owner?
What trust zone, exposure, and criticality is assigned to each component?
Who/what can read or write each data store and how is that access controlled?
How are backups, retention, and data integrity handled for each store?
What data classification does each store hold and how is it protected at rest (encryption, key management)?
What data stores exist (databases, caches, queues, file/object storage, secrets stores) and what does each hold?
How is each flow authenticated and authorized between endpoints?
What data classification and directionality applies to each flow, and which trust boundaries does it cross?
Is each data flow enumerated with source, destination, and the data it carries?
What protocol and transport protection (e.g. TLS) secures each flow in transit?
What are all entry points where data/requests enter the system (UIs, APIs, endpoints, ports, file uploads, message consumers)?
What is the exposure (internal vs internet-facing) and trust level of each entry point?
What authentication and input validation/sanitization gates each entry point?
What data classification leaves at each exit point and how is over-exposure/leakage prevented (output encoding, redaction)?
What destination and trust level does each exit point send to, and how is the transfer protected?
What are all exit points where data leaves the system (responses, outbound calls, logs, exports, notifications)?
How are credentials stored, rotated, recovered, and protected (hashing, secret storage, reset flows)?
What identity provider(s) and federation/trust relationships underpin authentication, and how is provider trust established?
What authentication mechanisms are used for each actor type (passwords, MFA, SSO/federation, certificates, API keys, service identities)?
How are sessions/tokens issued, validated, scoped, expired, and revoked?
How are delegation, impersonation, and on-behalf-of access governed, scoped, and audited?
Where are authorization checks enforced (gateway, service, data layer) and is enforcement consistent across UI, API, and background jobs?
What authorization model is used (RBAC, ABAC, ReBAC, ACLs) and where are policy decisions made (centralized PDP vs. scattered in code)?
How is object-level (per-resource) authorization enforced to prevent IDOR, and is it applied on every access path?
How are authorization policies and role/permission assignments reviewed, tested, and changed over time (policy lifecycle and recertification)?
What controls prevent horizontal and vertical privilege escalation, including default-deny and least-privilege role definitions?
What authentication methods exist for users and services (passwords, MFA, passwordless, SSO/federation) and what is the assurance level?
How do account recovery, password reset, and credential rotation work without becoming an authentication bypass?
What identity providers and federation/trust relationships exist (SAML/OIDC), and how is IdP trust, token validation, and account linking secured?
How are identities provisioned, deprovisioned, and joiner/mover/leaver transitions handled for users and service/machine identities?
How is privileged/administrative access controlled (MFA enforcement, just-in-time elevation, break-glass accounts)?
How are sessions and tokens issued, scoped, refreshed, expired, and revoked, and how is session fixation/hijacking mitigated?
What is exposed at the network edge (load balancers, gateways, WAF, DDoS protection) and what is the externally reachable attack surface?
How are ingress and egress controlled (firewalls, security groups, allowlists) and is outbound traffic restricted to prevent exfiltration?
How is internal/east-west traffic authenticated and encrypted (mTLS, service mesh, zero-trust) rather than implicitly trusted?
How is administrative and remote network access provided (VPN, bastion/jump hosts, private endpoints) and protected?
How is the network segmented into zones/tiers, and what trust boundaries separate public, internal, and sensitive segments?
Are approved, standard algorithms and primitives used (no home-grown crypto, no deprecated algorithms) with proper randomness sources?
How is data encrypted at rest (databases, storage, backups) and what algorithms and key strengths are used?
How is data protected in transit (TLS versions, cipher suites, certificate validation, mTLS) across all channels?
How are integrity, authenticity, and non-repudiation provided (signing, MACs, hashing of credentials) where required?
How are cryptographic keys generated, stored (KMS/HSM), rotated, and destroyed, and who can access them?
How is access to secrets authorized, scoped to least privilege, and audited (who/what can read each secret)?
How are secrets distributed to and injected into workloads at runtime without exposure in logs, images, or process listings?
How are secrets rotated and revoked, including on compromise, and are short-lived/dynamic credentials used where possible?
Where and how are secrets stored (vault/secret manager vs. code, config, env vars) and are any secrets hardcoded or in version control?
What controls protect business logic and workflows from abuse (rate limiting, anti-automation, state/transaction integrity)?
How do error handling and application logging avoid leaking sensitive data while capturing security-relevant events?
How are file uploads/downloads and SSRF-prone operations validated, sandboxed, and constrained?
How is untrusted input validated and sanitized, and how are injection classes (SQL, command, template, deserialization) prevented?
How is output encoding/escaping applied to prevent XSS and content-type confusion across rendering contexts?
What security headers and browser protections are set (CSP, HSTS, frame options, cookie flags) and CSRF defenses applied?
How are API clients authenticated (keys, OAuth2/OIDC, mTLS) and how are tokens scoped and validated per request?
Is there a complete API inventory covering versioning, deprecated/shadow/undocumented endpoints, and documentation accuracy?
How is broken object-level authorization (BOLA/IDOR) and object-property-level authorization prevented at API endpoints?
How are rate limiting, throttling, quotas, and resource-consumption limits enforced to prevent abuse and DoS?
How are API request/response schemas validated and mass-assignment, excessive data exposure, and parameter tampering prevented?
How are client-side dependencies, third-party scripts, and SDKs controlled (SRI, CSP, vetted libraries) against supply-chain tampering?
How is sensitive data stored and protected on the client (local/secure storage, cache, tokens) and cleared appropriately?
What platform hardening is applied for the client type (mobile: jailbreak/root detection, cert pinning; web: anti-clickjacking, DOM XSS defenses)?
How does the design account for the client being an untrusted environment, ensuring no security decisions rely solely on the client?
How are accounts/projects/VPCs structured to isolate environments and blast radius, including network and identity boundaries?
How are secure configuration baselines, drift detection, and IaC security scanning enforced across accounts/subscriptions?
How are cloud IAM roles, policies, and trust relationships scoped to least privilege, and how is privilege escalation/over-permissioning prevented?
How is cloud control-plane and data-plane activity logged, monitored, and protected from tampering (audit logs, threat detection)?
How are cloud resources protected from public exposure (storage buckets, databases, management interfaces, metadata service)?
How is the Kubernetes API server secured (RBAC, authentication, admission control) and least privilege enforced for service accounts?
How are container images sourced, scanned, signed, and verified, and how is base-image/registry trust maintained?
How are containers hardened at runtime (non-root, read-only FS, dropped capabilities, seccomp/AppArmor, no privileged mode)?
How are secrets and configuration handled in the orchestrator (encrypted etcd, external secret stores, no secrets in manifests)?
How are workloads isolated (network policies, namespaces, pod security standards) to limit lateral movement and node escape?
How are artifact repositories/registries secured and is artifact integrity verified between build, storage, and deploy stages?
How is build integrity and provenance ensured (isolated/ephemeral builders, reproducibility, SLSA-style attestation, artifact signing)?
How are software dependencies vetted, pinned, and scanned (SCA, lockfiles, SBOM) against known vulns and malicious/typosquatted packages?
What controls gate deployment to production (approvals, branch protection, code review, signed commits/artifacts verification)?
How is access to CI/CD systems, pipeline definitions, and runners controlled, and how are pipeline credentials scoped and protected?
How are vendors security-assessed before and during use (due diligence, certifications, contractual security/privacy obligations)?
How is vendor integration access scoped and isolated (least privilege, dedicated credentials, network restrictions) to limit blast radius?
What third parties/vendors are in use, what data and access does each receive, and is there a current inventory of these relationships?
How are vendor incidents, breaches, and SLA/security posture monitored over time, and how is secure offboarding/access revocation handled?
How is tenant data segregated and how is every data access scoped by tenant to prevent cross-tenant leakage?
What is the tenant isolation model (silo, pool, bridge) across compute, storage, and network, and where are shared resources?
How are per-tenant resource limits and quotas enforced to prevent noisy-neighbor and cross-tenant denial-of-service?
How is tenant context derived and enforced on every request, and how is tenant-ID spoofing or confused-deputy access prevented?
How are admin/support interfaces and tooling exposed and hardened (network restriction, separate auth, no public exposure) and their attack surface managed?
How are all admin/support/operator actions logged with individual accountability, and are logs tamper-resistant and reviewed?
How is privileged administrative/operator access granted, scoped to least privilege, and protected (strong MFA, just-in-time elevation)?
How are separation of duties and break-glass procedures enforced so no single operator can act unchecked on critical operations?
How can support staff access customer data/accounts (impersonation, debug tools), and what consent, scoping, and time-bounding controls apply?
Are logs centralized/aggregated, time-synchronized, and retained for a defined period sufficient for detection and investigation?
What detection rules/alerts exist for suspicious activity, and how are alerts triaged and escalated?
How does monitoring feed incident response (runbooks, on-call, metrics for detection coverage/MTTD)?
How are logs protected from tampering and unauthorized access (append-only/WORM, access controls, integrity verification)?
Which security-relevant events (authn, authz failures, privilege changes, config changes, data access) are logged, and is coverage complete across components?
Are secrets, credentials, and sensitive/PII data prevented from being written to logs (redaction/masking)?
How is each action reliably attributed to an authenticated identity, including delegated/service/impersonated actions?
Who can read or modify audit records, and is access to the audit trail itself audited and reviewed?
What actions produce an audit trail capturing who did what, when, from where, and to which resource?
For high-value or legally significant actions, what non-repudiation guarantees exist (signed receipts, cryptographic proof of origin)?
What mechanisms make audit records tamper-evident or tamper-proof (signing, hash chaining, immutable storage)?
What are the backup, restore, RTO/RPO objectives, and how are recovery procedures tested?
How does the system degrade gracefully (circuit breakers, timeouts, fail-safe defaults) when dependencies fail?
What rate limiting, quotas, throttling, and load-shedding protect the system under overload or abuse?
What redundancy and failover exist across components/zones/regions, and what are the failure domains and single points of failure?
What threats to availability are in scope (DoS/DDoS, resource exhaustion, dependency failure, data corruption) and how are they mitigated?
How is personal data anonymized/pseudonymized, and what controls govern third-party sharing and cross-border transfer?
What personal data is collected, where does it flow/reside, and how is it classified by sensitivity?
How are data subject rights (access, correction, portability, objection) supported and identity-verified?
Is data collection limited to a stated purpose with a lawful basis/consent, and is data minimization enforced?
What are the retention limits, and how are deletion and right-to-erasure requests fulfilled across all stores and backups?
Which regulatory, legal, and contractual frameworks (e.g. GDPR, HIPAA, PCI-DSS, SOC 2) apply to the system, and what is in scope?
How are required controls mapped to system features, and how is compliance evidenced and audited?
Who owns security/privacy policy, risk acceptance, and exception approval, and how is governance enforced?
What breach-notification and regulatory-reporting obligations apply, and what triggers/timelines/processes meet them?
How is enumeration completeness checked, and how is it kept current as the system and threat landscape change?
What methodology (STRIDE, attack trees, kill chain, etc.) is used to systematically enumerate threats per component and trust boundary?
For each trust boundary and data flow, what specific threats (spoofing, tampering, disclosure, DoS, EoP) have been identified?
Which threat actors (external attacker, malicious insider, compromised dependency, etc.) and their capabilities/motivations are considered?
Is each enumerated threat recorded with affected asset, attack vector, impact, and status (mitigated/accepted/open)?
What abuse/misuse cases describe how an attacker subverts intended functionality or business logic?
Is each abuse/misuse case linked to detective and preventive controls and acceptance criteria for handling it?
How could legitimate features be abused at scale (fraud, scraping, account takeover, spam, resource abuse) and what limits this?
How could authorized users or insiders misuse their legitimate access, and what controls detect/prevent it?
Who owns each control, how is its effectiveness measured/tested, and how are gaps tracked to remediation?
What security controls exist, classified as preventive, detective, and corrective, and where do they sit in the architecture?
Are controls layered (defense in depth) with no critical reliance on a single control, and are fail-safe defaults used?
Does each control trace to one or more threats it mitigates, and does each threat have at least one control or explicit acceptance?
Is each threat rated for likelihood and impact with documented rationale, and inherent vs residual risk distinguished?
How are risks prioritized and treated (mitigate, transfer, avoid, accept), and how is remediation tracked?
Who has authority to accept residual risk, and are accepted risks documented with justification and review dates?
What methodology scores risk (e.g. likelihood x impact, CVSS, DREAD) and how are levels defined consistently?
Where are the choke points/controls that break each attack path, and which paths remain unbroken?
What is the shortest/most-likely path to the system's crown-jewel assets, and how is that exposure reduced?
What end-to-end attack paths chain individual threats from entry point to high-value asset or impact?
How could an attacker move laterally or escalate privilege across trust boundaries once an initial foothold is gained?
How is each invariant enforced and where (code, schema, infra, policy), rather than relying on convention?
What security invariants must always hold (e.g. tenant isolation, no plaintext secrets at rest, authz on every access)?
How is each invariant continuously verified (tests, assertions, monitoring) and what happens on violation?
What is the security impact if a key assumption or dependency fails or is compromised, and how is that detected?
What external dependencies (services, libraries, infra, identity providers) is security inherited from, and what is their trust level?
What security assumptions does the model rely on (trusted networks, trusted callers, platform guarantees) and are they valid?
For each known gap, what is the planned remediation, owner, target date, or documented acceptance?
What is explicitly out of scope for this threat model, and why, so reviewers know the boundaries of coverage?
What known threats or weaknesses are currently unmitigated or only partially mitigated?
What artifacts demonstrate that key controls and invariants actually work as claimed (results, logs, attestations)?
How are validation findings, open items, and follow-up actions tracked to closure?
Who reviewed/validated the threat model, when, and how is it kept current with system changes?
What testing evidence (pentest, SAST/DAST, fuzzing, red team) backs the claimed mitigations and their effectiveness?
Where a primary control cannot be implemented, what compensating controls are in place and are they documented?
Is each identified threat mapped to one or more specific mitigating controls (preventive, detective, or corrective)?
What is the implementation status of each control (planned, in-progress, implemented, verified)?
Who owns each mitigation and what is its target remediation date or priority?
What is the residual risk after the mitigation is applied, and has it been explicitly accepted, transferred, or deferred?
How is each mitigation verified to be effective (test, scan, review, monitoring) rather than merely assumed?
Are breach-notification obligations and communication procedures (legal, customer, regulator) identified for this system?
What containment, eradication, and recovery capabilities exist (isolation, key/credential rotation, restore from backup)?
What detection and alerting exists to surface a security incident affecting this system, and who receives the alerts?
Are logs, audit trails, and evidence retained with sufficient fidelity and duration to support investigation and forensics?
Are incident roles, on-call ownership, and escalation paths defined for this system?
Are there documented runbooks/playbooks for the most likely incident scenarios for this system?
How is operational/administrative access granted, scoped (least privilege), reviewed, and audited?
Are backups taken, encrypted, access-controlled, and periodically restore-tested to a known RPO/RTO?
What change-management and configuration-drift controls govern production changes (review, approval, rollback)?
What security-relevant events are logged, where are logs centralized, and how is log integrity protected?
How are OS, runtime, and dependency patches tracked and applied, and what is the SLA for critical vulnerabilities?
How are operational secrets and keys stored, rotated, and revoked over the system's lifecycle?
How is the model assessed for adversarial examples, evasion, model extraction, and abuse (excessive cost/agency)?
What controls prevent leakage of sensitive/training data via model responses, embeddings, or memorization?
What is the provenance and integrity of pretrained models, weights, and ML dependencies (model supply chain)?
How are model outputs validated, filtered, and constrained before being trusted, displayed, or used to trigger actions?
How is the system protected against prompt injection and untrusted content reaching the model as instructions?
What is the provenance, integrity, and poisoning exposure of training/fine-tuning data?
What tamper-resistance/tamper-evidence and theft/loss protections exist for hardware components?
What environmental and hardware-supply-chain risks (counterfeit parts, untrusted manufacturing, disposal/decommission) are considered?
What is the exposure to peripheral/debug interfaces (JTAG, USB), removable media, and side-channel attacks?
What physical access controls protect devices, facilities, and ports, and what is the threat from physical access?
Are secure boot, firmware integrity, and trusted hardware roots of trust (TPM/HSM/secure element) in place?
Are flow annotations (protocol, direction, authentication, encryption) and their meanings defined in the legend?
Are diagram elements consistently labeled/keyed so they map unambiguously to the component, flow, and threat inventories?
Does the diagram define the notation/shapes for the core element types (process, data store, external entity, data flow)?
Is the notation for trust boundaries (and how crossings are marked) explicitly defined in the legend?
Does each component have a unique identifier, name, and type (process, data store, external entity)?
Does each component record its owner and its technology/runtime stack?
Does each component record its trust level/privilege and the data classification it handles?
Does each data flow record its authentication mechanism and encryption (in-transit) status?
Does each data flow record its source, destination, and direction?
Does each data flow record the protocol used and the classification/sensitivity of data carried?
Does each trust boundary record the controls enforced at the crossing (authentication, authorization, validation, filtering)?
Does each trust boundary enumerate the flows/components that cross it?
Does each trust boundary have an identifier and a clear description of the privilege/trust transition it represents?
Does each threat record its category (e.g. STRIDE) and a risk rating (likelihood/impact)?
Does each threat have a unique identifier, description, and the affected component/flow/boundary?
Does each threat link to its mitigation(s) and record a status (open, mitigated, accepted)?
